extracted.intended_audience: investors and corporate compliance officers (SEC filers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on what events U.S. public companies must report on Form 8-K and how to read those filings; covers the discrete numbered items (sections) that trigger current reports and the typical structure/content of an 8-K.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose: Notify investors of current events
rubrics_metrics.description: Form 8-K is used to notify investors of a current event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investors should always read any 8-K filings that are made by companies in which they are invested. These reports are often material to the company, and frequently contain information that will affect the share price.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of events that trigger Form 8-K
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of events that require an 8-K filing include signing/amending/terminating material definitive agreements, bankruptcies or receiverships, mine shutdowns/violations of mine safety laws, consummation of material asset acquisitions or sales, results of operations and financial condition, creation of certain financial obligations (incurrence of material debt), triggering events that accelerate material obligations (defaults), exit or disposal plans (layoffs, plant shutdowns, material change in services/outlets), material impairments, delisting or failing to satisfy listing requirements, unregistered equity sales (private placements), modifications to shareholder rights, change in accountants, determinations that previously issued financial statements cannot be relied upon, change in control, senior officer appointments and departures, director elections and departures, amendments to certificate/articles of incorporation or bylaws, changes in fiscal year, trading suspension under employee benefit plans, amendments or waivers of code of ethics, changes in shell company status, results of shareholder votes, disclosures applicable to issuers of asset-backed securities, disclosures necessary to comply with Regulation FD, other material events, and certain financial statements and other exhibits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the Official SEC Form 8-K Summary and annotated Form 8-K for links to rules and SEC guidance applicable to each event.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reading Form 8-K: structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Typically an 8-K filing will only have two major parts: the name and description of the event and any exhibits that are relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The name and description contains all information the company considers relevant to shareholders and the SEC; it has been deemed 'material' by the company. Exhibits may include financial statements, press releases, data tables, or other information referenced in the description of the event.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical items (pre-2004 correspondence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to August 23, 2004, 8-K items were filed under different item numbers (Item 1 through Item 12) covering similar topics (changes in control, acquisitions/dispositions, bankruptcy, changes in certifying accountant, results of operations, financial statements and exhibits, amendments to code of ethics, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historical numbering matters for older filings and research datasets; refer to historical item table when reviewing pre-2004 filings.
